name: Acquired Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum

criteria.description: Presence of yellowish papules and plaques with a cobblestone or plucked chicken skin appearance, primarily on the neck and flexural areas
Histological evidence of fragmented and calcified elastic fibers in the mid and deep dermis
Lack of mutations in ABCC6 gene and no family history of hereditary pseudoxanthoma elasticum
Presence of systemic conditions such as chronic renal failure or penicillamine therapy history

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cutaneous lesions plus histopathological confirmation of elastic fiber calcification and fragmentation, with exclusion of hereditary PXE
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of inherited PXE by genetic testing or family history

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish papular lesions with cobblestone texture on neck and flexures
searchTerms: yellow bumpy skin lesions on neck
raised yellow spots with cobblestone look
papules on neck and skin folds

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fragmentation and calcification of elastic fibers in dermis
searchTerms: broken and hardened elastic skin fibers

common.symptomName: Skin laxity and wrinkling in affected areas
Pruritus localized to affected skin regions

searchTerms: mild calcium deposits in peripheral arteries

occasional.notes: Less frequent than in hereditary PXE

occasional.symptomName: Intermittent claudication due to vascular involvement
searchTerms: leg pain when walking due to poor blood flow
intermittent leg cramps from vascular issues

occasional.symptomName: Calcification of elastic fibers in gastrointestinal tract
searchTerms: calcium deposits in gut elastic fibers

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness or reduced skin elasticity

rare.symptomName: Calcific uremic arteriolopathy in patients with renal failure
searchTerms: skin ulcers and calcification in kidney failure
calcific skin lesions in renal patients

rare.symptomName: Systemic arterial hypertension secondary to vascular calcification
searchTerms: high blood pressure from artery calcification
secondary hypertension due to vessel changes

laboratory: Histopathology showing fragmented and calcified elastic fibers in dermis
Normal ABCC6 gene sequencing (to exclude hereditary PXE)
imaging: Ophthalmologic imaging showing angioid streaks (less frequent)
genetic: Absence of pathogenic mutations in ABCC6 gene
other: History of exposure to causative agents such as penicillamine or chronic renal failure

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
Typically related to chronic sun exposure

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Vision changes or sudden visual loss
Signs of systemic vascular calcification causing ischemia
references: Neldner KH. Pseudoxanthoma elasticum. Clinical and genetic investigations. Arch Dermatol. 1988.
